chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Najjah from Muhammad ibn Ali from Mus'ab ibn Salam al-Taymi from Sa'd ibn Dharif from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

One who recites the Adhan for twenty years seeking reward, Allah will forgive him for the extent of his gaze and the extent of his voice in the sky, and everything, wet and dry, will testify to it, and for every person who prays with him in his mosque he will have a share, and for every person who prays with his voice he will have a good deed.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for reciting the Adhan for twenty years?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-A'mal, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the enduring merit of the Mu'adhin, noting that twenty years of consistent Adhan with Ihtisab (seeking reward) secures divine forgiveness proportional to the duration and vocal range. This tradition underscores the Mu'adhin's unique spiritual role, as every wet and dry entity testifies to his call, and he shares in the reward of every congregant praying in his mosque, reflecting the communal nature of worship in Shia jurisprudence.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakil who said it was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Yahya from Muhammad b. Ahmad from Muhammad b. Najayh from Muhammad b. Ali from Mus’ab b. Salam al-Taymi from Sa’d b. Dharif from Abi Ja’far (a.s.) who said:

“One who recites Azaan for ten years seeking reward from Allah, Allah would forgive him with the forgiveness equal to the number of times he looks at the sky and number of times his voice comes out. Everything, be it dry or wet will testify it. All those who hear this person and pray inside the mosque will also get a part of this reward.”
